note: Programs that built and ran clean on a real NVIDIA GPU (reference / pass-only / silent), copied unedited (except where `patched`) into cuda-projects/ready/<dir>/ with the headers and sibling sources they need. `removed_from_clone` lists what was taken out of cuda-projects/<dir>/ afterwards; `git -C cuda-projects/<dir> checkout -- <path>` restores any of it.

programs.patched: written for CUDA <= 12 -- not a bug in the program. In CUDA 13 both cudaMemPrefetchAsync(ptr, bytes, device) and cudaMemAdvise(ptr, bytes, advice, device) take a cudaMemLocation instead of a device id (the same break as in cuda-training-series hw6). The copy uses the CUDA 13 form at all ten call sites (4 cudaMemAdvise, 6 cudaMemPrefetchAsync).

written for CUDA <= 8: __any(pred) was removed for sm_70+ (ptxas: 'vote without .sync is not supported'). The copy uses __any_sync(0xffffffff, pred), the full-warp form that call site already assumes.
upstream bug: `return time < 0;` compares the libc function time() with 0, which g++ now rejects. The copy returns totalTime < 0 (always 0), the evident intent.

the vendored 2016 NVlabs/cub submodule collides with the CCCL cub that ships in CUDA 13 (#error CUB_NS_QUALIFIER); the copy includes the toolkit's <cub/cub.cuh> instead, and replaces cub::Sum() (removed in CCCL 3) with cuda::std::plus<int>() and the init value 0 that CCCL 3's Reduce now requires. The header warp_reduce.h calls __shfl_down() without a mask (removed for sm_70+); the build force-includes a one-function shim giving it the full-warp __shfl_down_sync form.

main.cu allocates head dim 64 and launches 32x16 threads for both kernels, but the kernels are compiled for head dim 128 with their own tiles (16x16 / 8x32) and blocks (16x16 / 128x8): out-of-bounds reads, 'illegal memory access' on any NVIDIA GPU. The copy uses d=128 and gives each kernel its own tile count, block and grid.

written for CUDA <= 12 -- not a bug in the program. cudaMemPrefetchAsync(ptr, bytes, device) was replaced in CUDA 13 by a form taking a cudaMemLocation and flags (nvcc 13: 'no suitable constructor exists to convert from int to cudaMemLocation'). The copy uses the CUDA 13 form.

written for CUDA <= 12 -- not a bug in the program. In CUDA 13 cudaMemPrefetchAsync(ptr, bytes, device) takes a cudaMemLocation and a flags argument instead of a device id (the same break as in cuda-training-series hw6). The copy uses the CUDA 13 form at all three call sites.
free() on the stack arrays h_A/h_B aborts with 'double free or corruption'; removed.
free() on the stack arrays h_input/h_output aborts with 'double free or corruption'; removed.

programs.patched: d_head/d_tail are declared `unsigned int` but used everywhere as device pointers (cudaMalloc(&d_head), atomicAdd(d_head, 1), *d_head); declared as `unsigned int*`.

two extern __shared__ kernels launched with no shared-memory size (the illegal address); the one-block scan assumes M*BINS <= 1024 (its own comment) but N=2^20 gives 65536; and the histogram is block-major where a radix sort needs digit-major. Copy: N=2^14 (M*BINS=1024), shared sizes passed, digit-major histogram and offsets.

programs.patched: the host wrapper uses `N` (lines 32, 37) where its parameter is `n`.

__syncthreads() inside `if (tid < s)` in both reductions: a barrier only some threads reach, which deadlocks (the 'timeout'); every thread reads mean[0] with no barrier after thread 0 writes it; and 256 threads for N=1024 averages only the first 256 elements. Copy: barriers moved out of the branch, a barrier before mean[0] is read, one block of N threads.
